definition: pgvector is a PostgreSQL extension that adds a vector column type and nearest-neighbour search, with client libraries for Python and Node.
details: Created by Andrew Kane in 2021; open source and available on most managed Postgres services.

explainer.lead: How to install pgvector, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
import psycopg
from pgvector.psycopg import register_vector

conn = psycopg.connect("dbname=app", autocommit=True)
conn.execute("CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector")
register_vector(conn)
conn.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS docs (id serial, body text, embedding vector(3))")
conn.execute("INSERT INTO docs (body, embedding) VALUES (%s, %s)", ("cats", [0.1, 0.9, 0.0]))
print(conn.execute("SELECT body FROM docs ORDER BY embedding <=> %s::vector LIMIT 1", ([0.1, 0.8, 0.1],)).fetchone())

explainer.inAi: Keep embeddings next to your app data and join them with ordinary SQL filters — no separate vector database.

tiers.eli5: It's like adding a new shelf to a familiar store that finds the items most similar to what you're holding.
tiers.practitioner: Created by Andrew Kane in 2021, it is open source and available on most managed Postgres services, letting teams run nearest-neighbour search alongside relational data.
